purpose: Machine-readable carrier capability, tactical-maturation and hull-state guard for the 1943-10-01 restart. Nominal aircraft capacity is explicitly separated from ready air group and deck-cycle combat output.
principles: Carrier combat power = hull/deck cycle + ready air group + pilot/crew median + search/strike/CAP coordination + geometry + damage/recovery state.
Nominal aircraft capacity is not combat-ready aircraft count and aircraft production does not create extra deck spots.
Hull survival does not prove current readiness, and aircraft type existence does not prove carrier-qualified unit conversion.
The 1942-43 Japanese tactical-learning effects are process improvements and variance reductions, not flat combat multipliers.
US old-carrier branch losses remain paid; late-1943 US power is new-build regeneration, not resurrection.

hull_state.allocation_at_restart: First-line core remains Pacific; central India package receives zero first-line carriers.
policy_notes: Chitose/Chiyoda remain seaplane tenders; no automatic carrier conversion.
Shinano is not converted to carrier under the current 1943 policy; Unryu-line quantity and Taiho-line quality remain separate construction policies.

drivers: Hiryu survival and larger surviving carrier/aircrew/deck/maintenance cadre
comparison of multiple carrier commands and deck crews
practices: overlapping/re-search search sectors with return margin
CAP altitude layers, relief timing, emergency launch and recovery schedule
avoid simultaneous maximization of fueled/armed/waiting aircraft on deck/hangar
pre-plan simultaneous evasive turns, local independent evasion and emergency dispersion/reassembly
cross-deck emergency recovery and aircraft redistribution after carrier damage
tactical_maturation_1942_43.rule: These are sensitivity bands for applicable trained formations. Do not stack them as one carrier-strength multiplier or apply when local crew, weather, comms or deck state do not support them.

first_line_fleet_carriers.state: alive; ship-specific 1943 deck-cycle and current air-group readiness must be resolved event-locally
first_line_fleet_carriers.rule: Do not infer current ready aircraft from opening main-six total or nominal design capacity.

Ryujo.mission_class: small fleet carrier under suitable wind/load; ship-specific damage/readiness still required

Zuiho.mission_class: light fleet carrier under suitable conditions

Shoho.conversion_clock: ~2-3 months earlier in opening technical baseline; current 1943 presence must follow branch fate/OOB, not this design card

Junyo_Hiyo.mission_class: low-speed medium fleet carriers; wind/load/recovery limitations remain
Junyo_Hiyo.rule: Do not treat as equal to first-line fast fleet carriers in every mission.

required_event_state: ready aircraft by role and variant

united_states.survivor: Wasp survives and is active by June 1943
united_states.regeneration: Multiple Essex/Independence-class fast-carrier groups with F6F-class aircraft are real combat factors by late Aug/Sep 1943.
united_states.rule: Actual October groups, air groups, deck readiness and task-group direction are event inputs. Do not reinsert lost legacy fast carriers.

britain.effect: Eastern Fleet modern-carrier depth is below historical; any eastern reinforcement is conditional on current hull, air-group, shipping, air-cover and command state.
